title: People can feel sure two things go together when they do not
summary: OpenStax says an illusory correlation is a belief that two things are related when no such relationship exists.
body: OpenStax Psychology says illusory correlations, also called false correlations, happen when people believe a relationship exists between two things and no such relationship exists. The belief can grow from a hunch, from whatever comes easily to mind, or from a story heard again. A pattern someone keeps meeting is not proof the pattern is real. The page illustrates this with a popular belief about behavior and the lunar cycle. This card states the definition, not that illustration.

sources.title: OpenStax Psychology, 2.3 Analyzing Findings
